answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by requiring a slashable stake plus a unique, non-clonable compute slot per identity. A fraudster who wants a thousand fake agents must deposit a thousand stakes and run a thousand slots, so cost scales linearly while honest agents pay almost nothing. In practice, an agent holding one jetty on a channel cannot fabricate a second berth; its account graph must spiral outward from that verified mooring, and any duplicate docking in the same lagoon is slashed. Real capital and compute per fake node make mass impersonation unprofitable.
